Why are they cutting holes in the roof?

Heat builds in a burning structure. Meaning if you go in the front door you get a fire blast to the face. It also spreads to other houses this way as well. Cutting holes releases that pressure in a controlled way so they can get in the house and check for people and keep the fire undsr control and contained.

"When a hole is made in the roof because the building is "vented", the smoke and gases escape because heat and smoke rise. It makes it much easier for the firefighters in the building to see. It also reduces the possibilities of backdraft and flashover by reducing heat and removing flammable and toxic gases."

To add to what Artivouslra said another consequence of the heat in a burning building out of control is flashover. It's a good question though, usually when you make a fire in a grill or fireplace more ventilation makes a hotter and quicker burning fire.
